title: Compose portable configuration into Vaporize and WCode Levels
description: Use Schema Universal configuration selections and Wrkstrm Core XCConfig services to project build inputs, receipt Vaporize builds, and give WCode a Windows-first Levels-style inspector and source-authorized editor without changing the existing macOS Xcode UI.
instructions: Update the Vaporize and WCode PRD and CUJs before implementation, including open, inspect, search, edit, preview, save, reopen, build, rollback, and failure journeys.
Consume versioned Schema Universal configuration and projection contracts and Wrkstrm Core XCConfig services through local-or-remote dependency policy; do not fork either model locally.

Project one portable selection into owned xcconfig and Swift build inputs and record manifest, platform, configuration, lane, feature status, adapter, output digest, Package.resolved, invocation, artifact, and runtime receipts separately.
Implement read-only Levels inspection and source editing as separate sibling services, each selected by feature policy and independently reversible.
Show effective values, winning and shadowed sources, line provenance, conditions, generated-versus-source authority, and typed diagnostics without reparsing text in the view.
Keep the macOS AppKit and Xcode paths unchanged; select the new WCode service only for the admitted Windows experiment until lane review approves otherwise.
Use CommonProcess for any tool execution, common-log for state and receipt logging, and separate Windows and macOS service test suites.
Reconcile the stale canonical-home record before claiming WCode has a standalone product home; until then this Vaporize repository is the operational WCode implementation boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: A Windows user opens an xcconfig-backed project in WCode and can inspect effective values and provenance without Xcode installed.
An unchanged file remains byte-identical and an edit changes only the selected source-authorized node.
Generated projections are read-only by default and identify their upstream typed manifest and digest.
The same feature selection produces equivalent declared behavior in xcconfig and Swift build inputs.
Vaporize receipts distinguish repeated attempts, no-change retries, failures, artifacts, installed runtimes, and human review authority.
Windows UI tests cover focus, keyboard input, pointer selection, copy/paste, scrolling, resizing, diagnostics, and rollback.
The existing macOS generator and UI suites remain unchanged and green before any release-lane promotion.
prerequisites: wrkstrm-core project configFiles parity contract and package
wrkstrm-core XcconfigCore lossless resolver contract and package
schema-universal cross-platform configuration projection schema release
explicit WCode read and edit feature-status policies
swift-universal/private/universal/kura-spaces/beads/bug-vaporize-wcode-canonical-home-record-drift-2026-08-27.beads-issue.su.json closes before standalone WCode ownership is claimed
prohibitions: Do not copy XCConfig or Schema Universal implementations into Vaporize.
Do not edit the production macOS view or generator to test the Windows sibling.
Do not use Foundation Process, PowerShell lifecycle scripts, print, or an untyped completion callback.
Do not log secret values or full private configuration files.
Do not claim Xcode conformance, signing, publication, or launch approval from a Windows WCode test.
